summary: The answer is the bitwise OR of all values, and any uninspected element may be the sole source of a result bit; one complete scan matches the resulting linear lower bound.

optimality.argument: For any array position, compare two inputs that agree everywhere inspected and differ only at that position, using zero in one input and a value with a previously absent bit in the other. Their maximum XOR answers differ, so a worst-case exact algorithm must inspect every element. Accumulating bitwise OR during one scan takes O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: A skipped element can be the only element containing a particular result bit, so omitting any position cannot distinguish otherwise identical arrays with different answers.
A single pass ORs each value into one accumulator, using constant auxiliary storage.
Authored fixtures cover zero, one element, duplicate bits, disjoint bits, overlapping values, repeated identical values, and both public examples; regression also exhausts small reachable submasks.
